summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of Addison’s disease, hypothyroidism, hypertension, and microscopic colitis was readmitted one week after prior discharge due to fatigue, salt craving, and diarrhea, consistent with an Addisonian crisis. She was treated with IV hydrocortisone and fluids in the emergency department, then transitioned to an oral prednisone taper. Her renal function, which was impaired due to dehydration (creatinine rising from 0.7 to 1.3), improved with rehydration and returned to baseline. Diarrhea resolved spontaneously, and abdominal pain—worsened after a right upper quadrant ultrasound—was managed with analgesia and remained stable with no new liver findings. Anemia was deemed chronic, likely related to underlying disease. She was discharged home in stable condition on a prednisone taper, with fludrocortisone restarted after the taper, and continuation of her baseline medications for thyroid, anxiety, GERD, and hypertension.
